subject: design-technology

moments.title: Bauhaus founded in Weimar
moments.body:
Gropius combines an arts and crafts school with a fine art academy. Teachers include Klee, Kandinsky, Itten and Albers.

The curriculum unites craft training with theoretical design.
moments.takeaway: Educational design was treated as a design problem in itself.

moments.title: Move to Dessau
moments.body: Gropius designs the new building. The school moves towards industrial production, with prototypes for tubular-steel furniture (Marcel Breuer).
moments.takeaway: Modernist design moved from craft sketches towards manufacturable products.

moments.title: Bauhaus closed
moments.body: Under political pressure the school is dissolved. Faculty emigrate to the US (Albers to Black Mountain and Yale; Mies van der Rohe to Chicago; Moholy-Nagy founds the New Bauhaus).
moments.takeaway: Forced migration spread an educational model across continents.

now.title: Bauhaus legacy today
now.body: Many product design and architecture curricula trace lineage to the Bauhaus. Critiques (e.g. Tom Wolfe's From Bauhaus to Our House, 1981) have queried its homogenising influence.
now.open_questions: What balances of craft and industry should design schools teach now? How do digital tools transform Bauhaus pedagogy?

reflection: A school operating for 14 years across three cities continues to shape global design education a century later.
